2) Any procurement timelines or PO cutover dates we should plan against?

Thanks — happy to iterate.

Hi all —

Quick sizing note after validating against Pulse's July traces (thanks Elaine for the sample). TL;DR: the proposed dedicated 10-GPU search pool should hit your target in average traffic, but sustained 3x spikes will increase 95th tail beyond 200ms unless we add either 2 GPU burst capacity or a caching layer in front of the long-context model for common prefixes. Details:

- Baseline assumptions used: 1.2M tokens/day, p50 request length 240 tokens, p95 request length 1.6k tokens (longer for conversation).
- Long-context inference: llama-3-70b-long on A100 gives ~1.7 tok/s per GPU at that seq length; effective concurrency on 10 GPUs = ~17 tok/s sustained, which matches baseline but not 3x spikes.
- Options to preserve SLO under spikes:
  - Add 2 warm standby GPUs (burst pool) that can absorb 2x concurrency during spikes (+$2,800/mo).
  - Implement prefix/KV caching for repeated user conversation starts (low infra cost, engineering lift).
  - Short-term: increase per-request timeout and fallback to 13B optimized model for very deep contexts (degrades LLM quality slightly).

Security/PII: Redwood Private + KMS + audit logs is supported. We can scope private control plane, customer-managed KMS, and full request logs for auditing; that will alter deployment logistics and may add setup fees. I will attach a short tech note in the SOW about the Private option.

Ive updated the capacity_estimate_Q3.xlsx to show the +2 burst GPUs delta and a line-item split:
- Reserved GPU uplift (8 GPUs): $9,400/mo
- Burst standby (2 GPUs): $2,800/mo
- Reranker add-on (4 x smaller GPUs): $1,200/mo
- Model/ops premium (long-context images/quant): $1,000/mo
= Total delta: $14,400/mo (if you take burst standby). Without burst standby the delta is $11,600/mo.

Happy to walk through these numbers on a 30-min call.

— Dylan
